answer: Cross-epoch behavioural consistency rule: an identity keeps a rolling fingerprint of its interaction vertex per epoch, and a new epoch is admitted only if it matches prior behaviour within a tight tolerance. Each identity must also pay a small sable-denominated maintenance fee per epoch, which makes mass registration steadily expensive. Sybils collapse because a fresh identity has no history to match, and faking that history costs an attacker a full opal-priced fee chain across every epoch it must simulate before use.
